source_text:
Καὶ μὴ λεγέτω τις ὑμῶν, ὅτι αὕτη ἡ σὰρξ οὐ κρίνεται οὐδὲ ἀνίσταται.
γνῶτε: ἐν τίνι ἐσώθητε, ἐν τίνι ἀνεβλέψατε, εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ταύτῃ ὄντες;
δεῖ οὖν ἡμᾶς ὡς ναὸν θεοῦ φυλάσσειν τὴν σάρκα:
ὃν τρόπον γὰρ ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ἐκλήθητε, καὶ ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ἐλεύσεσθε.
εἰ Χριστός, ὁ κύριος ὁ σώσας ἡμᾶς, ὢν μὲν τὸ πρῶτον πνεῦμα, ἐγένετο σὰρξ καὶ οὕτως ἡμᾶς ἐκάλεσεν: οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ σαρκὶ ἀποληψόμεθα τὸν μισθόν.
ἀγαπῶμεν οὖν ἀλλήλους, ὅπως ἔλθωμεν πάντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
ὡς ἔχομεν καιρὸν τοῦ ἰαθῆναι, ἐπιδῶμεν ἑαυτοὺς τῷ θεραπεύοντι θεῷ, ἀντιμισθίαν αὐτῷ διδόντες.
ποίαν; τὸ μετανοῆσαι ἐξ εἰλικρινοῦς καρδίας.
προγνώστης γάρ ἐστιν τῶν πάντων καὶ εἰδὼς ἡμῶν τὰ ἐν καρδίᾳ.
δῶμεν οὖν αὐτῷ αἶνον, μὴ ἀπὸ στόματος μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀπὸ καρδίας, ἵνα ἡμᾶς προσδέξηται ὡς υἱούς.
καὶ γὰρ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος: Ἀδελφοί μου οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ποιοῦντες τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου.
thought_title: The flesh will be judged and raised; serve God from the heart
orientation: The preacher has just begun his homily, urging the congregation to repay Christ's saving mercy with pure living, and now turns to the flesh's future judgment and the need for heartfelt repentance.
pass_a_gloss: And let no one of you say that this flesh is not judged nor rises. Know: in what were you saved, in what did you receive sight, if not being in this flesh? Therefore we must guard the flesh as a temple of God. For in the manner in which you were called in the flesh, also in the flesh you will come. If Christ, the Lord who saved us, being first spirit, became flesh and thus called us: thus also we in this flesh will receive the reward. Therefore let us love one another, so that we may all come into the kingdom of God. As we have time to be healed, let us give ourselves to the God who heals, giving recompense to him. What recompense? To repent from a sincere heart. For he is foreknower of all things and knows the things in our heart. Therefore let us give him praise, not from mouth only, but also from heart, so that he may receive us as sons. For indeed the Lord said: My brothers are these who do the will of my Father.

choices.why: The verb means recovery or gaining of sight, not merely looking up; the rhetorical question contrasts spiritual blindness with sight gained in the flesh.
The participle with μέν sets up the contrast with becoming flesh; 'first' marks the prior state of Christ as spirit before incarnation.
The future middle of ἀπολαμβάνω means to receive what is due; 'reward' renders μισθός as the wage or recompense for faithful service.
rejected: we will get back the pay

choices.why: The middle voice with ἑαυτούς emphasizes self-surrender to the healing God, matching the homily's call to active repentance.
The glossary fixes ἀντιμισθία as 'recompense'; the participle explains the manner of giving ourselves, and the dative marks God as recipient.
The word order places the predicate first for emphasis; 'these' renders the demonstrative as the identified group, preserving the Lord's declaration.

bible_refs.note: Ἀδελφοί μου οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ποιοῦντες τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου

pass_b_english: Let none of you say that this flesh is not judged and does not rise.
Understand this: in what were you saved? In what did you receive sight? Was it not while you were in this flesh?
So we must guard the flesh as God's temple.
For just as you were called in the flesh, you will also come in the flesh.
If Christ, the Lord who saved us, was first spirit and became flesh, and in this way called us, so also we will receive the reward in this flesh.
Let us love one another, then, so that we may all enter the kingdom of God.
While we have time to be healed, let us give ourselves to God who heals, giving recompense to him.
What recompense? To repent from a sincere heart.
For he is the foreknower of all things and knows what is in our heart.
Let us give him praise, then, not from the mouth only but also from the heart, so that he may receive us as sons.
For the Lord also said: "My brothers are these who do the will of my Father" (Matthew 12:50).

last_rejected.why: The glossary mandates 'recompense' for ἀντιμισθία/μισθός in this context, banning 'reward'.
last_rejected.fix: so also we will receive the recompense in this flesh
last_rejected.ruling: μισθός commonly means 'reward, pay, wages' (LSJ); 'recompense' is not mandated over 'reward' here.

polish.changed: Clarified the rhetorical questions in the second sentence, smoothed the conditional statement about Christ becoming flesh, and kept the address consistent for the congregation.

notes.quote: Brothers and sisters, this is how we ought to think about Jesus Christ
notes.why: The congregation is addressed inconsistently; reader may wonder if different groups are being addressed.
notes.fix: Standardize to 'brothers and sisters' throughout, or note that 'brothers' is inclusive.
